claims.text: Elemental Cr-coated zirconium-alloy cladding undergoes accelerated Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
Accelerated Cr–Zr interdiffusion is the primary cause of premature Cr-coating failure in high-temperature steam.
A 50–100 nm Hf interlayer can be deposited by PVD between the zirconium-alloy substrate and Cr coating.
The Hf interlayer will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion at high temperature.
The Hf interlayer will maintain the Cr coating's oxidation protection in subcritical water.
The Hf interlayer will maintain the Cr coating's oxidation protection in accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
Hf is refractory under the proposed conditions.
The Hf interlayer will form a stable and chemically compatible interfacial barrier.
The Hf barrier will restrict atomic diffusion between Cr and Zr.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will minimize premature Cr-coating failure in high-temperature steam.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the Hf interlayer will improve coating durability and mechanical and chemical integrity under normal and accident conditions.
Approximately 300°C pressurized subcritical water represents the proposed normal-operation test regime.
Approximately 1200°C steam represents the proposed short-term accident test regime.
The optimal Hf interlayer thickness remains unvalidated.
The long-term stability of the Hf interlayer under neutron irradiation and other reactor environments remains unvalidated.
